guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
The opposite trap is forced adulthood: perfect discipline, no visible needs, and very little joy or closeness. In that case the next adult act may be asking for help, expressing a preference, or letting a safe person see something imperfect—not tightening control again. Judge the strategy as well as the need. Wanting closeness is legitimate; demanding instant replies or punishing someone for needing space is not the same thing. The Guide helps find a workable way to meet the need without erasing either person.
brief:
- the opposite trap is forced adulthood: demanding perfect discipline of yourself, no visible needs, and very little joy or closeness (the trap is the demand, whether or not you manage it)
- if you're stuck there, the next adult act may be asking for help or saying what you'd prefer, not tightening control again (keep "may" and the scope: this is for someone stuck in forced adulthood)
- once a need does show, judge the strategy as well as the need: wanting closeness is legitimate; demanding instant replies or punishing someone for needing space isn't the same thing (keep "as well as")
- the Guide helps find a workable way to meet the need without erasing you or the other person (keep both people)
- the why a reader is missing (from the reviews, E170): the "needy" feeling is the old rule talking. Needs were among the things your little one learned to hide to keep belonging ("your little one learned bit by bit to hide that part of their authentic self which wasn't allowed, so they could keep belonging. They might still be doing it." in The Parent You Inherited), and forced adulthood is that inherited warden ("don't be needy") passing for the Guide, which is why tightening control feels like the grown-up thing. Use the why to carry the paragraph, not as a lesson at its end.
- context, not for the text: letting a safe person see something imperfect is already in When to Change the Strategy ("texting a friend that you're having a rough day instead of saying you're fine"), so leave it out.
- why the last version failed (Pangram, alone: AI 0.9987, all of it): "The opposite trap is forced adulthood, where you demand perfect discipline of yourself and have no visible needs, and very little joy or closeness. If you're stuck there, the next adult act may be asking for help or saying what you'd prefer, instead of tightening control again. Either of those can feel like turning into the needy one. Once a need does show, judge the strategy as well as the need: wanting closeness is legitimate, and demanding instant replies or punishing someone for needing space isn't the same thing. The Guide helps you find a workable way to meet the need without erasing you or the other person." It carries the guide's dense paragraph in the guide's order, each sentence handing off to the next, and its one reaction ("Either of those can feel like turning into the needy one.") wasn't enough.
